issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the Farm.animals collection and the solution does not follow the textual requirement. In the UML (problem_statement.md) Farm.animals is shown as a List<Animal>, but the textual Part 3 instructions state the aggregation must be realized using a Set implemented with a HashSet. The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This inconsistency (UML vs. text) in the specification and the solution's choice of List instead of the mandated Set can confuse students about which collection type to use and which behavior (uniqueness via Set) is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across the specification, template, and solution. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to show a Set<Animal> (and keep the textual instruction to use a HashSet), and update the solution/template to use a Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>(); or (B) change the textual instruction to require a List and update the wording about uniqueness accordingly. Prefer updating the UML to Set<Animal> and changing the solution to use HashSet to match the explicit textual requirement about uniqueness.

issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently specifies the Farm's animal collection type: the UML shows animals: List<Animal> while the textual task requires a Set implemented with a HashSet. The solution implements the collection as a List (ArrayList). This mismatch between 'List' and 'Set/HashSet' for the same conceptual entity (the Farm's animals collection) can confuse students about whether animals must be unique and which concrete collection to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection specification consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem UML and textual description to use List<Animal> (and change the textual mention of HashSet), or change the solution (and template guidance) to use Set<Animal> with new HashSet<>() and update the UML to show Set<Animal>. Ensure template Farm.java declares the animals field with the chosen type and initializes it accordingly (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>(); and adjust addAnimal/feedAllAnimals implementations).
